decision.observation: 10 mph, gear 1, two blue dots. The plain W beat drifted the car right off the gravel; it now sits on grass roughly two car widths right of the road, which sweeps left up-frame and climbs past pines and birches.
decision.hypothesis: The road lies clearly left and the car is only a couple of widths away, so a combined W+A beat at 10 mph should cross the grass and land it on the gravel while keeping most of the speed.
decision.memory: This left-hand bend is the same run-up seen earlier: plain throttle always pushes the car onto the right-side grass here, so the correction has to be steered rather than waited out. At 10 mph steers are cheap.
